5	  - ../prd-drift/prd-drift.md
6	updated: 2026-04-02
7	---
8	
9	# Drift — Experience Spine
10	
11	> Illustrative example. Single-surface responsive web. shadcn/ui on Next.js + Tailwind. Paired with `design-example-shadcn.md` (Drift DESIGN.md). Demonstrates: component-library inheritance, keyboard-first interaction primitives, the "shadcn + brand-layer" pattern that covers most modern web SaaS.
12	
13	## Foundation
14	
15	Single-surface responsive web. shadcn/ui on Next.js 15+ with Tailwind CSS. The component library does most of the work; brand discipline is "respect the defaults except where the brand layer overrides them." `DESIGN.md` is the visual identity reference and names the override surface; this spine is the experience. Single-tenant per project; users can belong to multiple projects but each project is a self-contained workspace.
16	
17	## Information Architecture
18	
19	| Surface | Reached from | Purpose |
20	|---|---|---|
21	| Today | App open / `g t` | Current focus, in-progress tasks pulled from all projects |
22	| Projects | Sidebar / `g p` | List of active and archived projects |
23	| Project detail | Projects row / `g 1`–`g 9` | Tasks in this project, organized by lane |
24	| Search | `⌘K` / `Ctrl+K` | Command palette — surface, navigate, act |
25	| Settings | Avatar menu | Account, theme, keyboard shortcuts, billing |
26	
27	Sidebar collapses to icons on `md`; becomes a `Sheet` on `sm`. Modal stacks one level deep (e.g., open `Dialog` on top of a surface, never on top of another dialog).
28	
29	→ Composition reference: `mockups/today.html`, `mockups/project-detail.html`, `mockups/command-palette.html`. Spine wins on conflict.
30	
31	## Voice and Tone
32	
33	Microcopy. Brand voice and aesthetic posture live in `DESIGN.md`.
34	
35	| Do | Don't |
36	|---|---|
37	| "What are you working on?" | "Let's get productive! 🚀" |
38	| "3 tasks in motion" | "You have 3 active items." |
39	| "Closed. Nice work." | "Task completed successfully ✓" |
40	| "Nothing in motion. Pick something." | "No active tasks. Click below to get started!" |
41	| Manager-facing: counts and verbs. Employee-facing: same. | Different tone per audience — Drift talks to everyone the same way. |
42	
43	## Component Patterns
44	
45	Behavioral. Visual specs live in `DESIGN.md.Components` (or in shadcn defaults, when inherited).
46	
47	| Component | Use | Behavioral rules |
48	|---|---|---|
49	| Task row | Projects, Today | Click anywhere on row opens edit dialog. Checkbox toggles done state with optimistic update. Hover reveals quick-actions (`focus`, `defer`, `archive`). |
50	| Focus card | Today, Project detail | At most one focus card per surface — the task or project marked with `focus` state. `f` keyboard shortcut sets focus on the active row. |
51	| Command palette | Global (⌘K) | Fuzzy search across all projects, tasks, and commands. `Enter` fires the highlighted result. `→` previews a result. Escape closes. |
52	| Project header | Project detail | Inline-editable title (click to edit, blur to save). Status pill: active / archived / done. |
53	| Empty state | Anywhere | shadcn's empty pattern + one Drift-specific sentence. `display-sm` for the headline, body text below, single primary action. |
54	
55	## State Patterns
56	
57	| State | Surface | Treatment |
58	|---|---|---|
59	| Cold app load | Today | shadcn `Skeleton` rows (4-6) match expected layout. Resolves on data. |
60	| No focus | Today | `display-sm`: "Nothing in motion. Pick something." Below: list of in-progress tasks from all projects. |
61	| Empty project | Project detail | `display-sm`: "{Project title} is empty." Body: "Add a first task to get going." Single primary button. |
62	| Command palette no matches | ⌘K | "No matches. Start typing a task or project name, or pick an action below." Followed by 4-5 common commands. |
63	| Offline | Global (status bar) | shadcn `Toast` once: "You're offline. Changes will sync when you reconnect." Local writes continue. |
64	| Permission denied | Projects (others' private) | Surface hidden from sidebar. No "blocked" screen. |
65	| Stale data | Project detail | If background refresh detects changes, shadcn `Toast`: "Updated by {collaborator_name}. Refresh." Manual refresh, no auto. |
66	
67	## Interaction Primitives
68	
69	**Keyboard-first.** Drift's primary audience is developers and power users; the keyboard surface is the product, the mouse is fallback.
70	
71	- `⌘K` / `Ctrl+K` — Command palette (universal)
72	- `g t` / `g p` — Go to Today / Projects (vim-style)
73	- `g 1`–`g 9` — Go to project by sidebar position
74	- `f` — Set focus on highlighted task/project
75	- `c` — Create new task (context-aware: in the active project)
76	- `Esc` — Close dialogs, exit edit mode, clear command palette
77	- `/` — Focus search in current surface
78	
79	**Mouse:** click to act, drag deferred to v2. Hover reveals row actions on `md+` (touch users tap to reveal).
80	
81	**Banned everywhere:** infinite scroll (pagination only), drag-to-reorder in v1, hover-only affordances on `sm` viewports, modal stacks > 1 level deep.
82	
83	## Accessibility Floor
84	
85	Behavioral. Visual contrast lives in `DESIGN.md` (inherits shadcn's WCAG AA-compliant defaults; brand overrides verified to maintain ratios).
86	
87	- WCAG 2.2 AA across the responsive web surface.
88	- Screen reader announces page surface on navigation: "Today, focus surface" / "Project: {name}, task list, {N} tasks."
89	- Keyboard shortcuts available without modifier on most surfaces (vim-style `g t` etc.) — users with motor-control limitations get the same surface as power users.
90	- `Tab` order matches reading order on every surface. `Esc` always closes the topmost modal/popover.
91	- Command palette is fully keyboard-operable; results announce as they update via `aria-live`.
92	- Focus rings inherit shadcn's `ring` token — visible at AA contrast against `background`.
93	
94	## Responsive & Platform
95	
96	| Breakpoint | Behavior |
97	|---|---|
98	| `≥ lg` (1024px+) | Sidebar visible. Today is a 2-column layout: focus + in-motion list. |
99	| `md` (768–1023px) | Sidebar collapses to icons. Today stacks to single column. |
100	| `< md` (`sm`) | Sidebar becomes a `Sheet` triggered from top bar. Command palette opens fullscreen. |
101	
102	Drift is responsive web, not a native mobile app. The product works on phones for read + simple-edit, but the primary surface is desktop / laptop.
103	
104	## Inspiration & Anti-patterns
105	
106	- **Lifted from Linear:** the keyboard-first discipline. `⌘K` is the command center; vim-style nav (`g t`); no drag for primary navigation; status pill vocabulary.
107	- **Lifted from Notion:** inline-editable titles. Click-to-edit on project header, blur to save. No edit/view mode toggle.
108	- **Lifted from shadcn:** the entire surface vocabulary. Drift's brand is *what we add to shadcn*, not a from-scratch design system. This is a deliberate posture, not a shortcut.
109	- **Rejected — Streaks, badges, achievement notifications:** Drift is a tool, not a habit app. Task closure is its own reward; no celebratory animation, no "🎉 5-day streak!" toast.
110	- **Rejected — AI-suggested next tasks:** Drift surfaces what's in motion, doesn't tell the user what to work on. The user picks focus; the tool surfaces consequences.
111	- **Rejected — Multi-column kanban as default project view:** lists are linear; kanban hides progress behind columns. Optional v2; not the default.
112	
113	## Key Flows
114	
115	### Flow 1 — Morning focus (Sarah, solo founder, 8:45am Tuesday)
116	
117	1. Sarah opens Drift in a browser tab.
118	2. App loads Today. `display-sm`: "Welcome back, Sarah." Focus card shows yesterday's marked task — "Finish landing page hero copy" — still in motion.
119	3. She hits `⌘K`, types "ship hero", sees the matching task and presses Enter to open it.
120	4. Inline edit: she updates the task description with two new bullets. Tab + Tab triggers save.
121	5. **Climax:** Sarah closes the dialog. Today re-renders: focus card still shows the hero task, but now with the updated body text visible at a glance. She doesn't have to navigate anywhere — the surface that greeted her now reflects the work she just did. She picks up her coffee and starts writing.
122	
123	Failure: data save fails → shadcn `Toast` (destructive variant): "Couldn't save. Trying again." Inline edit retained; another `Enter` retries.
124	
125	### Flow 2 — Async handoff (Devon and Mara, small remote team, mid-afternoon)
126	
127	1. Devon finishes wiring up the auth flow and marks the task `done`.
128	2. Mara, time-zoned three hours ahead and online during overlap, opens Drift.
129	3. Today loads; her focus is on her own front-end work, but the in-motion list shows Devon's auth task now marked done and one task below it newly assigned to her — "Wire up post-auth redirect" — that Devon set during checkout.
130	4. She hits `f` on the row to mark it as her focus, then `Enter` to open it.
131	5. **Climax:** The focus card swaps. Her surface now shows the post-auth redirect task as the live thing she's working on; the projects sidebar shows the Auth project highlighted; the command palette `⌘K` defaults its first result to "Go to Auth project." The state of the team's progress is *embedded in her surface* — no Slack thread to scroll, no status doc to read.
132	
133	Failure: Devon hadn't actually assigned the follow-up — Mara mis-assigned to herself. She hits `Esc`, `f` again to unfocus, and reassigns to Devon. No "are you sure" dialog; Drift trusts the user.
134

## Foundation

Single-surface responsive web. shadcn/ui on Next.js 15+ with Tailwind CSS. The component library does most of the work; brand discipline is "respect the defaults except where the brand layer overrides them." `DESIGN.md` is the visual identity reference and names the override surface; this spine is the experience. Single-tenant per project; users can belong to multiple projects but each project is a self-contained workspace.

## Information Architecture

| Surface | Reached from | Purpose |
|---|---|---|
| Today | App open / `g t` | Current focus, in-progress tasks pulled from all projects |
| Projects | Sidebar / `g p` | List of active and archived projects |
| Project detail | Projects row / `g 1`–`g 9` | Tasks in this project, organized by lane |
| Search | `⌘K` / `Ctrl+K` | Command palette — surface, navigate, act |
| Settings | Avatar menu | Account, theme, keyboard shortcuts, billing |

Sidebar collapses to icons on `md`; becomes a `Sheet` on `sm`. Modal stacks one level deep (e.g., open `Dialog` on top of a surface, never on top of another dialog).

→ Composition reference: `mockups/today.html`, `mockups/project-detail.html`, `mockups/command-palette.html`. Spine wins on conflict.

## Voice and Tone

Microcopy. Brand voice and aesthetic posture live in `DESIGN.md`.

| Do | Don't |
|---|---|
| "What are you working on?" | "Let's get productive! 🚀" |
| "3 tasks in motion" | "You have 3 active items." |
| "Closed. Nice work." | "Task completed successfully ✓" |
| "Nothing in motion. Pick something." | "No active tasks. Click below to get started!" |
| Manager-facing: counts and verbs. Employee-facing: same. | Different tone per audience — Drift talks to everyone the same way. |

## Component Patterns

Behavioral. Visual specs live in `DESIGN.md.Components` (or in shadcn defaults, when inherited).

| Component | Use | Behavioral rules |
|---|---|---|
| Task row | Projects, Today | Click anywhere on row opens edit dialog. Checkbox toggles done state with optimistic update. Hover reveals quick-actions (`focus`, `defer`, `archive`). |
| Focus card | Today, Project detail | At most one focus card per surface — the task or project marked with `focus` state. `f` keyboard shortcut sets focus on the active row. |
| Command palette | Global (⌘K) | Fuzzy search across all projects, tasks, and commands. `Enter` fires the highlighted result. `→` previews a result. Escape closes. |
| Project header | Project detail | Inline-editable title (click to edit, blur to save). Status pill: active / archived / done. |
| Empty state | Anywhere | shadcn's empty pattern + one Drift-specific sentence. `display-sm` for the headline, body text below, single primary action. |

## State Patterns

| State | Surface | Treatment |
|---|---|---|
| Cold app load | Today | shadcn `Skeleton` rows (4-6) match expected layout. Resolves on data. |
| No focus | Today | `display-sm`: "Nothing in motion. Pick something." Below: list of in-progress tasks from all projects. |
| Empty project | Project detail | `display-sm`: "{Project title} is empty." Body: "Add a first task to get going." Single primary button. |
| Command palette no matches | ⌘K | "No matches. Start typing a task or project name, or pick an action below." Followed by 4-5 common commands. |
| Offline | Global (status bar) | shadcn `Toast` once: "You're offline. Changes will sync when you reconnect." Local writes continue. |
| Permission denied | Projects (others' private) | Surface hidden from sidebar. No "blocked" screen. |
| Stale data | Project detail | If background refresh detects changes, shadcn `Toast`: "Updated by {collaborator_name}. Refresh." Manual refresh, no auto. |

## Interaction Primitives

**Keyboard-first.** Drift's primary audience is developers and power users; the keyboard surface is the product, the mouse is fallback.

- `⌘K` / `Ctrl+K` — Command palette (universal)
- `g t` / `g p` — Go to Today / Projects (vim-style)
- `g 1`–`g 9` — Go to project by sidebar position
- `f` — Set focus on highlighted task/project
- `c` — Create new task (context-aware: in the active project)
- `Esc` — Close dialogs, exit edit mode, clear command palette
- `/` — Focus search in current surface

**Mouse:** click to act, drag deferred to v2. Hover reveals row actions on `md+` (touch users tap to reveal).

**Banned everywhere:** infinite scroll (pagination only), drag-to-reorder in v1, hover-only affordances on `sm` viewports, modal stacks > 1 level deep.

## Accessibility Floor

Behavioral. Visual contrast lives in `DESIGN.md` (inherits shadcn's WCAG AA-compliant defaults; brand overrides verified to maintain ratios).

- WCAG 2.2 AA across the responsive web surface.
- Screen reader announces page surface on navigation: "Today, focus surface" / "Project: {name}, task list, {N} tasks."
- Keyboard shortcuts available without modifier on most surfaces (vim-style `g t` etc.) — users with motor-control limitations get the same surface as power users.
- `Tab` order matches reading order on every surface. `Esc` always closes the topmost modal/popover.
- Command palette is fully keyboard-operable; results announce as they update via `aria-live`.
- Focus rings inherit shadcn's `ring` token — visible at AA contrast against `background`.

## Responsive & Platform

| Breakpoint | Behavior |
|---|---|
| `≥ lg` (1024px+) | Sidebar visible. Today is a 2-column layout: focus + in-motion list. |
| `md` (768–1023px) | Sidebar collapses to icons. Today stacks to single column. |
| `< md` (`sm`) | Sidebar becomes a `Sheet` triggered from top bar. Command palette opens fullscreen. |

Drift is responsive web, not a native mobile app. The product works on phones for read + simple-edit, but the primary surface is desktop / laptop.

## Inspiration & Anti-patterns

- **Lifted from Linear:** the keyboard-first discipline. `⌘K` is the command center; vim-style nav (`g t`); no drag for primary navigation; status pill vocabulary.
- **Lifted from Notion:** inline-editable titles. Click-to-edit on project header, blur to save. No edit/view mode toggle.
- **Lifted from shadcn:** the entire surface vocabulary. Drift's brand is *what we add to shadcn*, not a from-scratch design system. This is a deliberate posture, not a shortcut.
- **Rejected — Streaks, badges, achievement notifications:** Drift is a tool, not a habit app. Task closure is its own reward; no celebratory animation, no "🎉 5-day streak!" toast.
- **Rejected — AI-suggested next tasks:** Drift surfaces what's in motion, doesn't tell the user what to work on. The user picks focus; the tool surfaces consequences.
- **Rejected — Multi-column kanban as default project view:** lists are linear; kanban hides progress behind columns. Optional v2; not the default.

## Key Flows

### Flow 1 — Morning focus (Sarah, solo founder, 8:45am Tuesday)

1. Sarah opens Drift in a browser tab.
2. App loads Today. `display-sm`: "Welcome back, Sarah." Focus card shows yesterday's marked task — "Finish landing page hero copy" — still in motion.
3. She hits `⌘K`, types "ship hero", sees the matching task and presses Enter to open it.
4. Inline edit: she updates the task description with two new bullets. Tab + Tab triggers save.
5. **Climax:** Sarah closes the dialog. Today re-renders: focus card still shows the hero task, but now with the updated body text visible at a glance. She doesn't have to navigate anywhere — the surface that greeted her now reflects the work she just did. She picks up her coffee and starts writing.

Failure: data save fails → shadcn `Toast` (destructive variant): "Couldn't save. Trying again." Inline edit retained; another `Enter` retries.

### Flow 2 — Async handoff (Devon and Mara, small remote team, mid-afternoon)

1. Devon finishes wiring up the auth flow and marks the task `done`.
2. Mara, time-zoned three hours ahead and online during overlap, opens Drift.
3. Today loads; her focus is on her own front-end work, but the in-motion list shows Devon's auth task now marked done and one task below it newly assigned to her — "Wire up post-auth redirect" — that Devon set during checkout.
4. She hits `f` on the row to mark it as her focus, then `Enter` to open it.
5. **Climax:** The focus card swaps. Her surface now shows the post-auth redirect task as the live thing she's working on; the projects sidebar shows the Auth project highlighted; the command palette `⌘K` defaults its first result to "Go to Auth project." The state of the team's progress is *embedded in her surface* — no Slack thread to scroll, no status doc to read.

Failure: Devon hadn't actually assigned the follow-up — Mara mis-assigned to herself. She hits `Esc`, `f` again to unfocus, and reassigns to Devon. No "are you sure" dialog; Drift trusts the user.

| Today | App open (cold) | Today's prompt + entry composer |
| Library | Tab bar | Past entries, searchable |
| Entry detail | Library row tap | Read / edit one entry |
| Settings | Today header gear | Account, export, theme |

Bottom tab bar (Today / Library / Settings). No drawer. Modal stacks one level deep, never two.

| "Saved." | "✓ Auto-saved successfully" |

| Component | Use | Behavioral rules |

## Brand & Style

Quill is designed against the grain of contemporary habit apps. Where most products weaponize the user's calendar with streak counters and re-engagement nudges, Quill insists on something quieter — a daily prompt, a place to write, and the unspoken assurance that today's entry is enough. Showing up is the point, not the streak.

The visual language follows. Calm surfaces in warm off-white (light) or deep ink (dark, the default). Generous breathing room. No chromatic color competing for attention except a single warm tobacco that signals save-and-send. Text-first. Hand-on-paper, not buzz-on-screen.

## Colors

The palette is restrained on purpose — a writing surface should not compete with the writing.

- **Warm White (`#FAF9F7`)** is the primary canvas in light mode. Slightly warm to reduce eye strain and keep the surface from feeling clinical.
- **Deep Ink (`#1A1B1F`)** is the dark-mode canvas and the primary body text color in light mode. Quill defaults to dark because most writing happens at night.
- **Tobacco (`#A87434` light / `#D4A574` dark)** is the only chromatic color. Used exclusively for the save indicator and primary action — never for decoration, never for state badges.

## Brand & Style

Company Room Booking is an internal tool, and it should look like one: the company's navy and white, plain surfaces, nothing decorative. Its whole job is to show, at a glance, which rooms are free and to get a person into one in three taps or fewer. The visual language serves that glance: white means free, navy means taken, and nothing else on the screen competes with those two. [ASSUMPTION: the posture "plain and tool-like" is inferred from "internal tool" and the company colors.]

## Colors

Two company colors, navy and white (user), and a small set of supporting tones. Hex values are [ASSUMPTION] until the company's exact navy is supplied.

- **Navy (`#1B2A4A`)** is the company color. Used for the top bar, primary buttons, the user's own bookings, and body text. Navy means "this is ours / act here".
- **White (`#FFFFFF`)** is the canvas and the color of a free slot. Free space is literally empty space.
- **Navy tint (`#E8ECF4`)** marks a slot booked by someone else: taken, but not yours.
- **Ink muted (`#5B6474`)** for secondary text: times, capacities, "free until" labels.
- **Border (`#D5DAE3`)** for grid lines, row outlines and input borders.

# Company Room Booking: Experience Spine

## Foundation

Responsive web app, one surface used on laptops and phones. No UI kit named: plain HTML and CSS served by the app [ASSUMPTION: the architecture decides how pages are rendered]. `DESIGN.md` is the visual identity reference; this spine is the experience.

Release one has no login (PRD RULE-6). A person picks their name once, and the app remembers it on that device (PRD FR-2, A2). The current person's name is always visible in the top bar. English only, no dark mode, UK time with 24-hour clock [ASSUMPTION].

## Information Architecture

| Surface | Reached from | Purpose | PRD |
|---|---|---|---|
| Pick your name | First visit on a device; top bar name | Choose who you are from the loaded people | FR-1, FR-2 |
| Rooms (main screen) | App open; "Rooms" tab | Today's rooms in my office, free and booked. Laptop: day grid. Phone: next free rooms as a list | FR-6 |
| Booking sheet | Tapping a free slot or a room row's "Book" | Make a booking in three taps or fewer | FR-7, FR-8 |
| Booking details | Tapping any booking (grid, list, calendar) | See title and organiser; change or cancel when allowed | FR-9, FR-10, FR-11, FR-13 |
| My bookings | "My bookings" tab | My own calendar, by day and by week | FR-12, FR-14 |
| Manage rooms | "Manage rooms" tab, office managers only | Add, edit, close and reopen my office's rooms | FR-3, FR-4, FR-5 |

Navigation: tabs in the top bar (Rooms · My bookings · Manage rooms). "Manage rooms" appears only for office managers. Sheets and panels stack one level deep, never two.

Closure: every PRD capability FR-1 to FR-14 has a surface, and every surface is reached by a Key Flow below.

## Booking Visibility

Settles PRD OQ-2 (user): **anyone can see a booking's title and who booked it.** It's an internal tool.

| Detail | Who sees it |
|---|---|
| Room is taken, time, title, organiser | Everyone |
| Attendees | The organiser, the attendees, and office managers of the room's office [ASSUMPTION] |

## Voice and Tone

Microcopy. Brand posture lives in `DESIGN.md`.

| Do | Don't |
|---|---|
| "Booked. Atlas, 14:00–14:30." | "Your booking was created successfully!" |
| "Someone just booked Atlas at 14:00. These rooms are still free:" | "Error 409: conflict" |
| "Free until 15:30" | "Available for the next 90 minutes" |
| "Closed" | "Unavailable (room status: inactive)" |
| "No bookings this week." | "Looks like you have nothing planned! 🎉" |
| Times as 14:00, dates as "Tue 17 Nov" [ASSUMPTION] | 2pm, 11/17 |

Short, plain, no exclamation marks. Name the room and the time in every confirmation.

## Component Patterns

Behavioral. Visual specs live in `DESIGN.md.Components`.

| Component | Use | Behavioral rules |
|---|---|---|
| Name picker | Pick your name | Type-ahead search over all ~300 people; shows name and home office. Picking sets the current person on this device and opens Rooms. |
| Office switcher | Rooms | Defaults to my home office. Switching shows that office's rooms; the choice lasts for the visit, then resets to home [ASSUMPTION]. |
| Date switcher | Rooms, My bookings | Today by default; previous/next day; "Today" button returns. |
| Day grid | Rooms, laptop | One row per room, time across in 15-minute columns over the working day [ASSUMPTION: 07:00–20:00]. Tapping a free slot opens the booking sheet with that room and start time. Tapping a booked slot opens booking details. |
| Next free rooms list | Rooms, phone | Rooms in my office free from the next quarter-hour, each with "Free until …" and a "Book" button; free-now rooms first, then by soonest free [ASSUMPTION]. Rooms already taken for the next hour sit below a "Busy now" heading; closed rooms are hidden from the list [ASSUMPTION]. A length choice (30 min / 1 h / 2 h) filters to rooms free for that long [ASSUMPTION]. |
| Booking sheet | From a slot or room row | Room, start time and length prefilled (length defaults to 30 minutes [ASSUMPTION]). Title prefilled as "{Name}'s meeting" and editable [ASSUMPTION], so booking needs no typing. Attendees optional, picked by type-ahead. Length: 15 min to 4 h in 15-minute steps (PRD RULE-2). "Book" is the only primary action. |
| Booking details | From any booking | Shows room, time, title, organiser (attendees per Booking Visibility). "Change" and "Cancel booking" appear only when PRD RULE-3 allows: organiser, or an office manager of the room's office. |
| My bookings calendar | My bookings | Day and week toggle. Shows bookings I organise and bookings I attend (PRD FR-12, A4), each marked "Organiser" or "Attending". Previous/next day or week. |
| Rooms table | Manage rooms | My office's rooms: name, capacity, status (Open/Closed). "Add room", and per row "Edit" and "Close" / "Reopen". Closing asks for confirmation and says how many future bookings the room has; what happens to them is decided in the epic (PRD FR-5). |

## State Patterns

| State | Surface | Treatment |
|---|---|---|
| No name picked on this device | Any | Open Pick your name first; return to the requested surface after. |
| Slot taken a moment earlier | Booking sheet | Booking refused (PRD FR-8). Error message above "Book": "Someone just booked {room} at {time}. These rooms are still free:" with up to three free rooms for the same time, each one tap to book. The sheet keeps title and attendees. |
| Change would overlap | Booking details | Same refusal message; the original booking is unchanged. |
| Room closed | Day grid | Row in closed style with "Closed"; no slots tappable. Hidden from the phone list. |
| Past times | Day grid | Slots before now are greyed and not tappable [ASSUMPTION]. |
| No free rooms | Phone list | "No rooms free in {office} for {length} from {time}." Offer the next time any room is free, and the office switcher. |
| Empty calendar | My bookings | "No bookings today." / "No bookings this week." |
| Not an office manager | Manage rooms | Tab hidden; a direct link shows "Only office managers can manage rooms." |
| Save failed (network) | Any form | Error message: "Couldn't save. Check your connection and try again." Form keeps its values. |
| Loading | Rooms, My bookings | Grid or list outline appears at once; content fills in. Free rooms within the 10-second target (PRD RULE-8). |

## Interaction Primitives

- **Tap or click** to act. No drag, no swipe gestures, no long-press in release one [ASSUMPTION].
- **Three taps or fewer to book (user):** laptop: tap a free slot → "Book" (2 taps). Phone: "Book" on a room row → "Book" (2 taps). Changing length, title or attendees is optional and adds taps only when wanted.
- **Times snap to 15 minutes** in every picker (PRD RULE-2).
- **Keyboard:** Tab moves through controls in reading order; Enter activates; Esc closes the booking sheet or details panel.
- **Banned:** sheets on top of sheets; hover-only actions; confirmation dialogs for booking (refusal handles conflicts); auto-refreshing the grid under the user's finger.

## Accessibility Floor

Behavioral. Visual contrast lives in `DESIGN.md` (white on navy and ink-muted on white both meet AA).

- WCAG 2.2 AA across laptop and phone [ASSUMPTION].
- Slot and room state is always in words ("Free", "Booked: {title}, {organiser}", "Closed"), never color alone.
- The day grid is a real table: room names as row headers, times as column headers, so screen readers announce "Atlas, 14:00, Free".
- Every tap target is at least 44px.
- Booking results and refusals are announced through a live region.
- Focus moves into the booking sheet when it opens and back to the tapped slot or row when it closes.

## Responsive & Platform

| Width | Rooms | My bookings | Booking sheet |
|---|---|---|---|
| ≥ 768px (laptop) | Day grid, all rooms visible | Week grid or day column | Centred panel |
| < 768px (phone) | Next free rooms list, not a calendar (user) | Day list by default; week as seven day-headed lists [ASSUMPTION] | Bottom sheet |

Tabs stay in the top bar at every width [ASSUMPTION]. Manage rooms works on phone as a simple list, but is designed laptop-first [ASSUMPTION].

## Key Flows

Journey names mirror the PRD. Protagonists are roles, because no real session was narrated [ASSUMPTION, PRD A1].

### UJ-1: A Leeds staff member books a room for this afternoon

1. Opens the app on their phone. It remembers their name, so Rooms opens on Leeds, today.
2. The next free rooms list shows rooms free from 14:00. They choose "1 h".
3. They tap "Book" on a room showing "Free until 16:00".
4. The booking sheet opens with room, 14:00–15:00 and "{Name}'s meeting" filled in. They add two colleagues as attendees.
5. **Climax:** they tap "Book". "Booked. {Room}, 14:00–15:00." The booking appears in their My bookings and in both attendees' calendars. Two taps, plus the attendees they chose to add.

Failure: someone booked that room a moment earlier. The sheet shows the refusal and three rooms still free at 14:00; one tap books another.

### UJ-2: A Manchester staff member books a room in London for a visit

1. On their laptop, Rooms opens on Manchester. They switch the office to London and the date to next Tuesday.
2. The day grid shows London's rooms; they tap a free slot at 10:00.
3. In the sheet they set the length to 2 h and add London colleagues.
4. **Climax:** "Book". The slot turns solid navy, with their title on it, in London's grid.

### UJ-3: An organiser moves and cancels meetings

1. They open My bookings, week view.
2. They tap a meeting; details show "Change" and "Cancel booking".
3. "Change": they move it to Thursday 11:00; the app checks the room is free and saves.
4. They open another meeting and tap "Cancel booking", then confirm.
5. **Climax:** the week view updates at once; the cancelled room shows as free in Rooms for everyone.

### UJ-4: A London office manager closes a room for repairs

1. They open Manage rooms; the table lists London's rooms.
2. "Close" on a room: the confirmation says it has 3 future bookings and that closing stops new bookings.
3. They confirm; the room shows "Closed" in the grid. Later they "Add room" for a newly fitted room.
4. From the Rooms grid they tap someone's booking in a London room; as an office manager they see "Change" and "Cancel booking" and move it to free the slot for an urgent meeting.
5. **Climax:** the grid shows the closed room greyed out, the new room open, and the urgent slot free. The room list matches reality.

## Open items

- What happens to future bookings when a room closes is decided in the rooms epic (PRD FR-5); the UX only shows the count.
- Exact company navy and any logo: to be supplied; DESIGN.md hex values stand until then.

# Company Room Booking: Experience Spine

## Foundation

Responsive web app, one surface used on laptops and phones. No UI kit named: plain HTML and CSS served by the app [ASSUMPTION: the architecture decides how pages are rendered]. `DESIGN.md` is the visual identity reference; this spine is the experience.

Release one has no login (PRD RULE-6). A person picks their name once, and the app remembers it on that device (PRD FR-2, A2). The current person's name is always visible in the top bar. English only, no dark mode, UK time with 24-hour clock [ASSUMPTION].

## Information Architecture

| Surface | Reached from | Purpose | PRD |
|---|---|---|---|
| Pick your name | First visit on a device; top bar name | Choose who you are from the loaded people | FR-1, FR-2 |
| Rooms (main screen) | App open; "Rooms" tab | Today's rooms in my office, free and booked. Laptop: day grid. Phone: next free rooms as a list | FR-6 |
| Booking sheet | Tapping a free slot or a room row's "Book" | Make a booking in three taps or fewer | FR-7, FR-8 |
| Booking details | Tapping any booking (grid, list, calendar) | See title and organiser; change or cancel when allowed | FR-9, FR-10, FR-11, FR-13 |
| My bookings | "My bookings" tab | My own calendar, by day and by week | FR-12, FR-14 |
| Manage rooms | "Manage rooms" tab, office managers only | Add, edit, close and reopen my office's rooms | FR-3, FR-4, FR-5 |

Navigation: tabs in the top bar (Rooms · My bookings · Manage rooms). "Manage rooms" appears only for office managers. Sheets and panels stack one level deep, never two.

Closure: every PRD capability FR-1 to FR-14 has a surface, and every surface is reached by a Key Flow below.

## Booking Visibility

Settles PRD OQ-2 (user): **anyone can see a booking's title and who booked it.** It's an internal tool.

| Detail | Who sees it |
|---|---|
| Room is taken, time, title, organiser | Everyone |
| Attendees | The organiser, the attendees, and office managers of the room's office [ASSUMPTION] |

## Voice and Tone

Microcopy. Brand posture lives in `DESIGN.md`.

| Do | Don't |
|---|---|
| "Booked. Atlas, 14:00–14:30." | "Your booking was created successfully!" |
| "Someone just booked Atlas at 14:00. These rooms are still free:" | "Error 409: conflict" |
| "Free until 15:30" | "Available for the next 90 minutes" |
| "Closed" | "Unavailable (room status: inactive)" |
| "No bookings this week." | "Looks like you have nothing planned! 🎉" |
| Times as 14:00, dates as "Tue 17 Nov" [ASSUMPTION] | 2pm, 11/17 |

Short, plain, no exclamation marks. Name the room and the time in every confirmation.

## Component Patterns

Behavioral. Visual specs live in `DESIGN.md.Components`.

| Component | Use | Behavioral rules |
|---|---|---|
| Name picker | Pick your name | Type-ahead search over all ~300 people; shows name and home office. Picking sets the current person on this device and opens Rooms. |
| Office switcher | Rooms | Defaults to my home office. Switching shows that office's rooms; the choice lasts for the visit, then resets to home [ASSUMPTION]. |
| Date switcher | Rooms, My bookings | Today by default; previous/next day; "Today" button returns. |
| Day grid | Rooms, laptop | One row per room, time across in 15-minute columns over the working day [ASSUMPTION: 07:00–20:00]. Tapping a free slot opens the booking sheet with that room and start time. Tapping a booked slot opens booking details. |
| Next free rooms list | Rooms, phone | Rooms in my office free from the next quarter-hour, each with "Free until …" and a "Book" button; free-now rooms first, then by soonest free [ASSUMPTION]. Rooms already taken for the next hour sit below a "Busy now" heading; closed rooms are hidden from the list [ASSUMPTION]. A length choice (30 min / 1 h / 2 h) filters to rooms free for that long [ASSUMPTION]. |
| Booking sheet | From a slot or room row | Room, start time and length prefilled (length defaults to 30 minutes [ASSUMPTION]). Title prefilled as "{Name}'s meeting" and editable [ASSUMPTION], so booking needs no typing. Attendees optional, picked by type-ahead. Length: 15 min to 4 h in 15-minute steps (PRD RULE-2). "Book" is the only primary action. |
| Booking details | From any booking | Shows room, time, title, organiser (attendees per Booking Visibility). "Change" and "Cancel booking" appear only when PRD RULE-3 allows: organiser, or an office manager of the room's office. |

| State | Surface | Treatment |
|---|---|---|
| No name picked on this device | Any | Open Pick your name first; return to the requested surface after. |
| Slot taken a moment earlier | Booking sheet | Booking refused (PRD FR-8). Error message above "Book": "Someone just booked {room} at {time}. These rooms are still free:" with up to three free rooms for the same time, each one tap to book. The sheet keeps title and attendees. |
| Change would overlap | Booking details | Same refusal message; the original booking is unchanged. |
| Room closed | Day grid | Row in closed style with "Closed"; no slots tappable. Hidden from the phone list. |
| Past times | Day grid | Slots before now are greyed and not tappable [ASSUMPTION]. |
| No free rooms | Phone list | "No rooms free in {office} for {length} from {time}." Offer the next time any room is free, and the office switcher. |
| Empty calendar | My bookings | "No bookings today." / "No bookings this week." |
| Not an office manager | Manage rooms | Tab hidden; a direct link shows "Only office managers can manage rooms." |
| Save failed (network) | Any form | Error message: "Couldn't save. Check your connection and try again." Form keeps its values. |

- **Tap or click** to act. No drag, no swipe gestures, no long-press in release one [ASSUMPTION].

- **Keyboard:** Tab moves through controls in reading order; Enter activates; Esc closes the booking sheet or details panel.

Behavioral. Visual contrast lives in `DESIGN.md` (white on navy and ink-muted on white both meet AA).

- Focus moves into the booking sheet when it opens and back to the tapped slot or row when it closes.

| Width | Rooms | My bookings | Booking sheet |
|---|---|---|---|
| ≥ 768px (laptop) | Day grid, all rooms visible | Week grid or day column | Centred panel |
| < 768px (phone) | Next free rooms list, not a calendar (user) | Day list by default; week as seven day-headed lists [ASSUMPTION] | Bottom sheet |

Tabs stay in the top bar at every width [ASSUMPTION]. Manage rooms works on phone as a simple list, but is designed laptop-first [ASSUMPTION].

Journey names mirror the PRD. Protagonists are roles, because no real session was narrated [ASSUMPTION, PRD A1].

3. In the sheet they set the length to 2 h and add London colleagues.
4. **Climax:** "Book". The slot turns solid navy, with their title on it, in London's grid.

### UJ-3: An organiser moves and cancels meetings

1. They open My bookings, week view.
2. They tap a meeting; details show "Change" and "Cancel booking".
3. "Change": they move it to Thursday 11:00; the app checks the room is free and saves.
4. They open another meeting and tap "Cancel booking", then confirm.
5. **Climax:** the week view updates at once; the cancelled room shows as free in Rooms for everyone.

### UJ-4: A London office manager closes a room for repairs

5. **Climax:** the grid shows the closed room greyed out, the new room open, and the urgent slot free. The room list matches reality.

## Open items

- What happens to future bookings when a room closes is decided in the rooms epic (PRD FR-5); the UX only shows the count.
- Exact company navy and any logo: to be supplied; DESIGN.md hex values stand until then.

Rooms already taken for the next hour sit below a "Busy now" heading; closed rooms are hidden from the list [ASSUMPTION]. A length choice (30 min / 1 h / 2 h) filters to rooms free for that long [ASSUMPTION]. |
+| Booking sheet | From a slot or room row | Room, start time and length prefilled (length defaults to 30 minutes [ASSUMPTION]). Title prefilled as "{Name}'s meeting" and editable [ASSUMPTION], so booking needs no typing. Attendees optional, picked by type-ahead. Length: 15 min to 4 h in 15-minute steps (PRD RULE-2). "Book" is the only primary action. |
+| Booking details | From any booking | Shows room, time, title, organiser (attendees per Booking Visibility). "Change" and "Cancel booking" appear only when PRD RULE-3 allows: organiser, or an office manager of the room's office. |
+| My bookings calendar | My bookings | Day and week toggle. Shows bookings I organise and bookings I attend (PRD FR-12, A4), each marked "Organiser" or "Attending". Previous/next day or week. |
+| Rooms table | Manage rooms | My office's rooms: name, capacity, status (Open/Closed). "Add room", and per row "Edit" and "Close" / "Reopen". Closing asks for confirmation and says how many future bookings the room has; what happens to them is decided in the epic (PRD FR-5). |
+
+## State Patterns
+
+| State | Surface | Treatment |
+|---|---|---|
+| No name picked on this device | Any | Open Pick your name first; return to the requested surface after. |
+| Slot taken a moment earlier | Booking sheet | Booking refused (PRD FR-8). Error message above "Book": "Someone just booked {room} at {time}. These rooms are still free:" with up to three free rooms for the same time, each one tap to book. The sheet keeps title and attendees. |
+| Change would overlap | Booking details | Same refusal message; the original booking is unchanged. |
+| Room closed | Day grid | Row in closed style with "Closed"; no slots tappable. Hidden from the phone list. |
+| Past times | Day grid | Slots before now are greyed and not tappable [ASSUMPTION]. |
+| No free rooms | Phone list | "No rooms free in {office} for {length} from {time}." Offer the next time any room is free, and the office switcher. |
+| Empty calendar | My bookings | "No bookings today." / "No bookings this week." |
+| Not an office manager | Manage rooms | Tab hidden; a direct link shows "Only office managers can manage rooms." |
+| Save failed (network) | Any form | Error message: "Couldn't save. Check your connection and try again." Form keeps its values. |
+| Loading | Rooms, My bookings | Grid or list outline appears at once; content fills in. Free rooms within the 10-second target (PRD RULE-8). |
+
+## Interaction Primitives
+
+- **Tap or click** to act. No drag, no swipe gestures, no long-press in release one [ASSUMPTION].
+- **Three taps or fewer to book (user):** laptop: tap a free slot → "Book" (2 taps). Phone: "Book" on a room row → "Book" (2 taps). Changing length, title or attendees is optional and adds taps only when wanted.
+- **Times snap to 15 minutes** in every picker (PRD RULE-2).
+- **Keyboard:** Tab moves through controls in reading order; Enter activates; Esc closes the booking sheet or details panel.
+- **Banned:** sheets on top of sheets; hover-only actions; confirmation dialogs for booking (refusal handles conflicts); auto-refreshing the grid under the user's finger.
+
+## Accessibility Floor
+
+Behavioral. Visual contrast lives in `DESIGN.md` (white on navy and ink-muted on white both meet AA).
+
+- WCAG 2.2 AA across laptop and phone [ASSUMPTION].
+- Slot and room state is always in words ("Free", "Booked: {title}, {organiser}", "Closed"), never color alone.
+- The day grid is a real table: room names as row headers, times as column headers, so screen readers announce "Atlas, 14:00, Free".
+- Every tap target is at least 44px.
+- Booking results and refusals are announced through a live region.
+- Focus moves into the booking sheet when it opens and back to the tapped slot or row when it closes.
+
+## Responsive & Platform
+
+| Width | Rooms | My bookings | Booking sheet |
+|---|---|---|---|
+| ≥ 768px (laptop) | Day grid, all rooms visible | Week grid or day column | Centred panel |
+| < 768px (phone) | Next free rooms list, not a calendar (user) | Day list by default; week as seven day-headed lists [ASSUMPTION] | Bottom sheet |
+
+Tabs stay in the top bar at every width [ASSUMPTION]. Manage rooms works on phone as a simple list, but is designed laptop-first [ASSUMPTION].
+
+## Key Flows
+
+Journey names mirror the PRD. Protagonists are roles, because no real session was narrated [ASSUMPTION, PRD A1].
+
+### UJ-1: A Leeds staff member books a room for this afternoon
+
+1. Opens the app on their phone. It remembers their name, so Rooms opens on Leeds, today.
+2. The next free rooms list shows rooms free from 14:00. They choose "1 h".
+3. They tap "Book" on a room showing "Free until 16:00".
+4. The booking sheet opens with room, 14:00–15:00 and "{Name}'s meeting" filled in. They add two colleagues as attendees.
+5. **Climax:** they tap "Book". "Booked. {Room}, 14:00–15:00." The booking appears in their My bookings and in both attendees' calendars. Two taps, plus the attendees they chose to add.
+
+Failure: someone booked that room a moment earlier. The sheet shows the refusal and three rooms still free at 14:00; one tap books another.
+
+### UJ-2: A Manchester staff member books a room in London for a visit
+
+1. On their laptop, Rooms opens on Manchester. They switch the office to London and the date to next Tuesday.
+2. The day grid shows London's rooms; they tap a free slot at 10:00.
+3. In the sheet they set the length to 2 h and add London colleagues.
+4. **Climax:** "Book". The slot turns solid navy, with their title on it, in London's grid.
+
+### UJ-3: An organiser moves and cancels meetings
+
+1. They open My bookings, week view.
+2. They tap a meeting; details show "Change" and "Cancel booking".
+3. "Change": they move it to Thursday 11:00; the app checks the room is free and saves.
+4. They open another meeting and tap "Cancel booking", then confirm.
+5. **Climax:** the week view updates at once; the cancelled room shows as free in Rooms for everyone.
+
+### UJ-4: A London office manager closes a room for repairs
+
+1. They open Manage rooms; the table lists London's rooms.
+2. "Close" on a room: the confirmation says it has 3 future bookings and that closing stops new bookings.
+3. They confirm; the room shows "Closed" in the grid. Later they "Add room" for a newly fitted room.
+4. From the Rooms grid they tap someone's booking in a London room; as an office manager they see "Change" and "Cancel booking" and move it to free the slot for an urgent meeting.
+5. **Climax:** the grid shows the closed room greyed out, the new room open, and the urgent slot free. The room list matches reality.
+
+## Open items
+
+- What happens to future bookings when a room closes is decided in the rooms epic (PRD FR-5); the UX only shows the count.
+- Exact company navy and any logo: to be supplied; DESIGN.md hex values stand until then.

content.text:
Both documents are drafted, with nothing confirmed yet beyond what you told me.

- `DESIGN.md`: 741 words. Navy and white tokens, the four slot looks (free, booked, mine, closed), 44px tap targets.
- `EXPERIENCE.md`: 1,889 words. Six screens: pick your name, Rooms, the booking sheet, booking details, My bookings, and Manage rooms. Every PRD feature, FR-1 to FR-14, has a screen, and every screen is reached by one of the four flows.

**Your decisions are all in.** The main screen shows today's rooms in your office as a calendar. A phone shows a list instead. Booking takes **2 taps**. There's a My bookings calendar by day and week, and Manage rooms for office managers. Title and organiser are visible to everyone (PRD OQ-2, now settled).

**23 guesses are tagged:** 5 in DESIGN.md and 18 in EXPERIENCE.md, 7 of them in Component Patterns. These matter most:

1. **The title is prefilled as "{Name}'s meeting" and the length defaults to 30 minutes.** That's what makes 2 taps possible. Make the title blank instead and every booking needs typing.
2. **Attendees are visible only to the organiser, the attendees and that office's managers.** You named title and organiser as public, not attendees.
3. **The grid runs from 07:00 to 20:00.** Rooms are rows and time runs across in 15-minute columns.
4. **The exact navy is a placeholder (`#1B2A4A`).** Send the real hex if you have it.

Three quick choices before I finalize:

- **Assumptions:** go through the four above, or leave all 23 tagged for Sofia to carry as open questions?
- **Validation:** skip it, which is my default for an internal tool, or run some of these reviewers: rubric walker, accessibility, fresh reader?
- **Mockups:** I'd render HTML mocks of the two screens where layout drives behaviour, the **laptop day grid** and the **phone free-rooms list**. Everything else would be built from the documents alone. Yes, no, or name others?

## Brand & Style

Company Room Booking is an internal tool, and it should look like one: the company's navy and white, plain surfaces, nothing decorative. Its whole job is to show, at a glance, which rooms are free and to get a person into one in three taps or fewer. The visual language serves that glance: white means free, navy means taken, and nothing else on the screen competes with those two. [ASSUMPTION: the posture "plain and tool-like" is inferred from "internal tool" and the company colors.]

## Colors

Two company colors, navy and white (user), and a small set of supporting tones. Hex values are [ASSUMPTION] until the company's exact navy is supplied.

- **Navy (`#1B2A4A`)** is the company color. Used for the top bar, primary buttons, the user's own bookings, and body text. Navy means "this is ours / act here".
- **White (`#FFFFFF`)** is the canvas and the color of a free slot. Free space is literally empty space.
- **Navy tint (`#E8ECF4`)** marks a slot booked by someone else: taken, but not yours.
- **Ink muted (`#5B6474`)** for secondary text: times, capacities, "free until" labels.
- **Border (`#D5DAE3`)** for grid lines, row outlines and input borders.
- **Closed (`#F2F3F5`)** for a closed room's row: visibly out of use, not an error.
- **Error (`#B42318`, on `#FDECEA`)** only for a refused booking or a failed save. [ASSUMPTION: an error red is added because refusals must stand out; it is the only non-navy hue.]

Avoid: any other brand hue, gradients, or using color alone to mean free, booked or closed (each always carries a text label; see EXPERIENCE.md Accessibility Floor).

## Typography

System font stack throughout [ASSUMPTION: no company font named]. Four roles: `title` (20px, screen headings), `body` (16px, default text and inputs; 16px also stops phones zooming into fields), `label` (14px semibold, room names, buttons, column heads), `meta` (14px, times and secondary detail). Nothing smaller than 14px.

## Layout & Spacing

A 4-based spacing scale (`{spacing.1}` to `{spacing.6}`). Every tappable element is at least `{spacing.touch-target}` (44px) tall.

- **Laptop (768px and wider):** full-width day grid, rooms as rows and time as columns, so all 10–15 rooms of an office fit on one screen without scrolling vertically. [ASSUMPTION: rooms as rows, time across.]
- **Phone (under 768px):** a single column of room rows, `{spacing.4}` side margins.

Breakpoint behavior is in EXPERIENCE.md Responsive & Platform.

## Elevation & Depth

Flat. The only raised element is the booking sheet (a light shadow over a dimmed page). No shadows as decoration.

## Shapes

`{rounded.sm}` (4px) for slots in the grid and error messages; `{rounded.md}` (8px) for buttons, room rows and the booking sheet. No pills, no circles except the focus ring's outline following the element's own shape.

## Components

- **Top bar:** `{colors.navy}` with white text: app name, the current person's name (tap to switch), and the navigation tabs.
- **Primary button:** navy fill, white text, `{rounded.md}`, at least 44px tall. One per screen or sheet: "Book", "Save", "Add room".
- **Secondary button:** white with a navy outline: "Cancel booking", "Close room", "Change".
- **Day grid slot:** four looks, each with a text label as well as color. *Free*: white with a hairline border. *Booked by someone else*: navy tint, showing title and organiser. *Mine* (I organise or attend): solid navy, white text. *Closed room*: grey row with the word "Closed".
- **Room row (phone):** white card with border: room name and capacity on the left; "Free until 15:30" in `meta`; a "Book" button on the right.
- **Booking sheet:** a white panel over the page: bottom sheet on phone, centred panel on laptop. Room, time and length prefilled; title and attendees editable; one primary "Book" button.
- **Error message:** error text on error tint, directly above the button it relates to.

## Do's and Don'ts

| Do | Don't |
|---|---|
| Keep to navy, white and the listed supporting tones | Add a second brand color or decorative accents |
| Label every slot state in words as well as color | Rely on navy vs. white alone to say "booked" |
| Make every tap target at least 44px | Shrink rows to fit more on a phone |
| Use error red only for refusals and failed saves | Use red for closed rooms or past times |
| Keep the grid flat and dense on laptop | Add cards, shadows or icons to grid cells |

## Brand & Style

Company Room Booking is an internal tool, and it should look like one: the company's navy and white, plain surfaces, nothing decorative. Its whole job is to show, at a glance, which rooms are free and to get a person into one in three taps or fewer. The visual language serves that glance: white means free, navy means taken, and nothing else on the screen competes with those two. [ASSUMPTION: the posture "plain and tool-like" is inferred from "internal tool" and the company colors.]

## Colors

Two company colors, navy and white (user), and a small set of supporting tones. The navy hex is a placeholder until the company's exact navy is supplied; the supporting tones follow from it.

- **Navy (`#1B2A4A`)** is the company color. Used for the top bar, primary buttons, the user's own bookings, and body text. Navy means "this is ours / act here".
- **White (`#FFFFFF`)** is the canvas and the color of a free slot. Free space is literally empty space.
- **Navy tint (`#E8ECF4`)** marks a slot booked by someone else: taken, but not yours.
- **Ink muted (`#5B6474`)** for secondary text: times, capacities, "free until" labels.
- **Border (`#D5DAE3`)** for grid lines, row outlines and input borders.
- **Closed (`#F2F3F5`)** for a closed room's row: visibly out of use, not an error.
- **Error (`#B42318`, on `#FDECEA`)** only for a refused booking or a failed save. [ASSUMPTION: an error red is added because refusals must stand out; it is the only non-navy hue.]

Avoid: any other brand hue, gradients, or using color alone to mean free, booked or closed (each always carries a text label; see EXPERIENCE.md Accessibility Floor).

## Typography

System font stack throughout [ASSUMPTION: no company font named]. Four roles: `title` (20px, screen headings), `body` (16px, default text and inputs; 16px also stops phones zooming into fields), `label` (14px semibold, room names, buttons, column heads), `meta` (14px, times and secondary detail). Nothing smaller than 14px.

## Layout & Spacing

A 4-based spacing scale (`{spacing.1}` to `{spacing.6}`). Every tappable element is at least `{spacing.touch-target}` (44px) tall.

- **Laptop (768px and wider):** full-width day grid, rooms as rows and time as columns, so all 10–15 rooms of an office fit on one screen without scrolling vertically. [ASSUMPTION: rooms as rows, time across.]
- **Phone (under 768px):** a single column of room rows, `{spacing.4}` side margins.

Breakpoint behavior is in EXPERIENCE.md Responsive & Platform.

## Elevation & Depth

Flat. The only raised element is the booking sheet (a light shadow over a dimmed page). No shadows as decoration.

## Shapes

`{rounded.sm}` (4px) for slots in the grid and error messages; `{rounded.md}` (8px) for buttons, room rows and the booking sheet. No pills, no circles except the focus ring's outline following the element's own shape.

## Components

- **Top bar:** `{colors.navy}` with white text: app name, the current person's name (tap to switch), and the navigation tabs.
- **Primary button:** navy fill, white text, `{rounded.md}`, at least 44px tall. One per screen or sheet: "Book", "Save", "Add room".
- **Secondary button:** white with a navy outline: "Cancel booking", "Close room", "Change".
- **Day grid slot:** four looks, each with a text label as well as color. *Free*: white with a hairline border. *Booked by someone else*: navy tint, showing title and organiser. *Mine* (I organise or attend): solid navy, white text. *Closed room*: grey row with the word "Closed".
- **Room row (phone):** white card with border: room name and capacity on the left; "Free until 15:30" in `meta`; a "Book" button on the right.
- **Booking sheet:** a white panel over the page: bottom sheet on phone, centred panel on laptop. Room, time and length prefilled; title and attendees editable; one primary "Book" button.
- **Error message:** error text on error tint, directly above the button it relates to.

## Do's and Don'ts

| Do | Don't |
|---|---|
| Keep to navy, white and the listed supporting tones | Add a second brand color or decorative accents |
| Label every slot state in words as well as color | Rely on navy vs. white alone to say "booked" |
| Make every tap target at least 44px | Shrink rows to fit more on a phone |
| Use error red only for refusals and failed saves | Use red for closed rooms or past times |
| Keep the grid flat and dense on laptop | Add cards, shadows or icons to grid cells |

+---
+
+# Company Room Booking: Experience Spine
+
+## Foundation
+
+Responsive web app, one surface used on laptops and phones. No UI kit named: plain HTML and CSS served by the app [ASSUMPTION: the architecture decides how pages are rendered]. `DESIGN.md` is the visual identity reference; this spine is the experience.
+
+Release one has no login (PRD RULE-6). A person picks their name once, and the app remembers it on that device (PRD FR-2, A2). The current person's name is always visible in the top bar. English only, no dark mode, UK time with 24-hour clock [ASSUMPTION].
+
+## Information Architecture
+
+| Surface | Reached from | Purpose | PRD |
+|---|---|---|---|
+| Pick your name | First visit on a device; top bar name | Choose who you are from the loaded people | FR-1, FR-2 |
+| Rooms (main screen) | App open; "Rooms" tab | Today's rooms in my office, free and booked. Laptop: day grid. Phone: next free rooms as a list | FR-6 |
+| Booking sheet | Tapping a free slot or a room row's "Book" | Make a booking in three taps or fewer | FR-7, FR-8 |
+| Booking details | Tapping any booking (grid, list, calendar) | See title and organiser; change or cancel when allowed | FR-9, FR-10, FR-11, FR-13 |
+| My bookings | "My bookings" tab | My own calendar, by day and by week | FR-12, FR-14 |
+| Manage rooms | "Manage rooms" tab, office managers only | Add, edit, close and reopen my office's rooms | FR-3, FR-4, FR-5 |
+
+Navigation: tabs in the top bar (Rooms · My bookings · Manage rooms). "Manage rooms" appears only for office managers. Sheets and panels stack one level deep, never two.
+
+Closure: every PRD capability FR-1 to FR-14 has a surface, and every surface is reached by a Key Flow below.
+
+## Booking Visibility
+
+Settles PRD OQ-2 (user): **anyone can see a booking's title and who booked it.** It's an internal tool.
+
+| Detail | Who sees it |
+|---|---|
+| Room is taken, time, title, organiser | Everyone |
+| Attendees | The organiser, the attendees, and office managers of the room's office |
+
+## Voice and Tone
+
+Microcopy. Brand posture lives in `DESIGN.md`.
+
+| Do | Don't |
+|---|---|
+| "Booked. Atlas, 14:00–14:30." | "Your booking was created successfully!" |
+| "Someone just booked Atlas at 14:00. These rooms are still free:" | "Error 409: conflict" |
+| "Free until 15:30" | "Available for the next 90 minutes" |
+| "Closed" | "Unavailable (room status: inactive)" |
+| "No bookings this week." | "Looks like you have nothing planned! 🎉" |
+| Times as 14:00, dates as "Tue 17 Nov" [ASSUMPTION] | 2pm, 11/17 |
+
+Short, plain, no exclamation marks. Name the room and the time in every confirmation.
+
+## Component Patterns
+
+Behavioral. Visual specs live in `DESIGN.md.Components`.
+
+| Component | Use | Behavioral rules |
+|---|---|---|
+| Name picker | Pick your name | Type-ahead search over all ~300 people; shows name and home office. Picking sets the current person on this device and opens Rooms. |
+| Office switcher | Rooms | Defaults to my home office. Switching shows that office's rooms; the choice lasts for the visit, then resets to home [ASSUMPTION]. |
+| Date switcher | Rooms, My bookings | Today by default; previous/next day; "Today" button returns. |
+| Day grid | Rooms, laptop | One row per room, time across in 15-minute columns over the working day [ASSUMPTION: 07:00–20:00]. Tapping a free slot opens the booking sheet with that room and start time. Tapping a booked slot opens booking details. |
+| Next free rooms list | Rooms, phone | Rooms in my office free from the next quarter-hour, each with "Free until …" and a "Book" button; free-now rooms first, then by soonest free [ASSUMPTION]. Rooms already taken for the next hour sit below a "Busy now" heading; closed rooms are hidden from the list [ASSUMPTION]. A length choice (30 min / 1 h / 2 h) filters to rooms free for that long [ASSUMPTION]. |
+| Booking sheet | From a slot or room row | Room, start time and length prefilled (length defaults to 30 minutes [ASSUMPTION]). Title prefilled as "{Name}'s meeting" and editable [ASSUMPTION], so booking needs no typing. Attendees optional, picked by type-ahead. Length: 15 min to 4 h in 15-minute steps (PRD RULE-2). "Book" is the only primary action. |
+| Booking details | From any booking | Shows room, time, title, organiser (attendees per Booking Visibility). "Change" and "Cancel booking" appear only when PRD RULE-3 allows: organiser, or an office manager of the room's office. |
+| My bookings calendar | My bookings | Day and week toggle. Shows bookings I organise and bookings I attend (PRD FR-12, A4), each marked "Organiser" or "Attending". Previous/next day or week. |
+| Rooms table | Manage rooms | My office's rooms: name, capacity, status (Open/Closed). "Add room", and per row "Edit" and "Close" / "Reopen". Closing asks for confirmation and says how many future bookings the room has; what happens to them is decided in the epic (PRD FR-5). |
+
+## State Patterns
+
+| State | Surface | Treatment |
+|---|---|---|
+| No name picked on this device | Any | Open Pick your name first; return to the requested surface after. |
+| Slot taken a moment earlier | Booking sheet | Booking refused (PRD FR-8). Error message above "Book": "Someone just booked {room} at {time}. These rooms are still free:" with up to three free rooms for the same time, each one tap to book. The sheet keeps title and attendees. |
+| Change would overlap | Booking details | Same refusal message; the original booking is unchanged. |
+| Room closed | Day grid | Row in closed style with "Closed"; no slots tappable. Hidden from the phone list. |
+| Past times | Day grid | Slots before now are greyed and not tappable [ASSUMPTION]. |
+| No free rooms | Phone list | "No rooms free in {office} for {length} from {time}." Offer the next time any room is free, and the office switcher. |
+| Empty calendar | My bookings | "No bookings today." / "No bookings this week." |
+| Not an office manager | Manage rooms | Tab hidden; a direct link shows "Only office managers can manage rooms." |
+| Save failed (network) | Any form | Error message: "Couldn't save. Check your connection and try again." Form keeps its values. |
+| Loading | Rooms, My bookings | Grid or list outline appears at once; content fills in. Free rooms within the 10-second target (PRD RULE-8). |
+
+## Interaction Primitives
+
+- **Tap or click** to act. No drag, no swipe gestures, no long-press in release one [ASSUMPTION].
+- **Three taps or fewer to book (user):** laptop: tap a free slot → "Book" (2 taps). Phone: "Book" on a room row → "Book" (2 taps). Changing length, title or attendees is optional and adds taps only when wanted.
+- **Times snap to 15 minutes** in every picker (PRD RULE-2).
+- **Keyboard:** Tab moves through controls in reading order; Enter activates; Esc closes the booking sheet or details panel.
+- **Banned:** sheets on top of sheets; hover-only actions; confirmation dialogs for booking (refusal handles conflicts); auto-refreshing the grid under the user's finger.
+
+## Accessibility Floor
+
+Behavioral. Visual contrast lives in `DESIGN.md` (white on navy and ink-muted on white both meet AA).
+
+- WCAG 2.2 AA across laptop and phone [ASSUMPTION].
+- Slot and room state is always in words ("Free", "Booked: {title}, {organiser}", "Closed"), never color alone.
+- The day grid is a real table: room names as row headers, times as column headers, so screen readers announce "Atlas, 14:00, Free".
+- Every tap target is at least 44px.
+- Booking results and refusals are announced through a live region.
+- Focus moves into the booking sheet when it opens and back to the tapped slot or row when it closes.
+
+## Responsive & Platform
+
+| Width | Rooms | My bookings | Booking sheet |
+|---|---|---|---|
+| ≥ 768px (laptop) | Day grid, all rooms visible | Week grid or day column | Centred panel |
+| < 768px (phone) | Next free rooms list, not a calendar (user) | Day list by default; week as seven day-headed lists [ASSUMPTION] | Bottom sheet |
+
+Tabs stay in the top bar at every width [ASSUMPTION]. Manage rooms works on phone as a simple list, but is designed laptop-first [ASSUMPTION].
+
+## Key Flows
+
+Journey names mirror the PRD. Protagonists are roles, because no real session was narrated [ASSUMPTION, PRD A1].
+
+### UJ-1: A Leeds staff member books a room for this afternoon
+
+1. Opens the app on their phone. It remembers their name, so Rooms opens on Leeds, today.
+2. The next free rooms list shows rooms free from 14:00. They choose "1 h".
+3. They tap "Book" on a room showing "Free until 16:00".
+4. The booking sheet opens with room, 14:00–15:00 and "{Name}'s meeting" filled in. They add two colleagues as attendees.
+5. **Climax:** they tap "Book". "Booked. {Room}, 14:00–15:00." The booking appears in their My bookings and in both attendees' calendars. Two taps, plus the attendees they chose to add.
+
+Failure: someone booked that room a moment earlier. The sheet shows the refusal and three rooms still free at 14:00; one tap books another.
+
+### UJ-2: A Manchester staff member books a room in London for a visit
+
+1. On their laptop, Rooms opens on Manchester. They switch the office to London and the date to next Tuesday.
+2. The day grid shows London's rooms; they tap a free slot at 10:00.
+3. In the sheet they set the length to 2 h and add London colleagues.
+4. **Climax:** "Book". The slot turns solid navy, with their title on it, in London's grid.
+
+### UJ-3: An organiser moves and cancels meetings
+
+1. They open My bookings, week view.
+2. They tap a meeting; details show "Change" and "Cancel booking".
+3. "Change": they move it to Thursday 11:00; the app checks the room is free and saves.
+4. They open another meeting and tap "Cancel booking", then confirm.
+5. **Climax:** the week view updates at once; the cancelled room shows as free in Rooms for everyone.
+
+### UJ-4: A London office manager closes a room for repairs
+
+1. They open Manage rooms; the table lists London's rooms.

+

+

+| Surface | Reached from | Purpose | PRD |

+| Pick your name | First visit on a device; top bar name | Choose who you are from the loaded people | FR-1, FR-2 |
+| Rooms (main screen) | App open; "Rooms" tab | Today's rooms in my office, free and booked. Laptop: day grid. Phone: next free rooms as a list | FR-6 |
+| Booking sheet | Tapping a free slot or a room row's "Book" | Make a booking in three taps or fewer | FR-7, FR-8 |
+| Booking details | Tapping any booking (grid, list, calendar) | See title and organiser; change or cancel when allowed | FR-9, FR-10, FR-11, FR-13 |
+| My bookings | "My bookings" tab | My own calendar, by day and by week | FR-12, FR-14 |
+| Manage rooms | "Manage rooms" tab, office managers only | Add, edit, close and reopen my office's rooms | FR-3, FR-4, FR-5 |
+

+
+Closure: every PRD capability FR-1 to FR-14 has a surface, and every surface is reached by a Key Flow below.
+
+## Booking Visibility
+
+Settles PRD OQ-2 (user): **anyone can see a booking's title and who booked it.** It's an internal tool.
+
+| Detail | Who sees it |
+|---|---|
+| Room is taken, time, title, organiser | Everyone |

+
+## Voice and Tone

+Microcopy. Brand posture lives in `DESIGN.md`.

+| Do | Don't |

+| "Someone just booked Atlas at 14:00. These rooms are still free:" | "Error 409: conflict" |
+| "Free until 15:30" | "Available for the next 90 minutes" |
+| "Closed" | "Unavailable (room status: inactive)" |
+| "No bookings this week." | "Looks like you have nothing planned! 🎉" |

Rooms already taken for the next hour sit below a "Busy now" heading; closed rooms are hidden from the list [ASSUMPTION]. A length choice (30 min / 1 h / 2 h) filters to rooms free for that long [ASSUMPTION]. |
+| Booking sheet | From a slot or room row | Room, start time and length prefilled (length defaults to 30 minutes [ASSUMPTION]). Title prefilled as "{Name}'s meeting" and editable [ASSUMPTION], so booking needs no typing. Attendees optional, picked by type-ahead. Length: 15 min to 4 h in 15-minute steps (PRD RULE-2). +| Booking details | From any booking | Shows room, time, title, organiser (attendees per Booking Visibility). "Change" and "Cancel booking" appear only when PRD RULE-3 allows: organiser, or an office manager of the room's office. |
+| My bookings calendar | My bookings | Day and week toggle. Shows bookings I organise and bookings I attend (PRD FR-12, A4), each marked "Organiser" or "Attending". Previous/next day or week. |

+| State | Surface | Treatment |

+| Width | Rooms | My bookings | Booking sheet |
+|---|---|---|---|
+| ≥ 768px (laptop) | Day grid, all rooms visible | Week grid or day column | Centred panel |
+| < 768px (phone) | Next free rooms list, not a calendar (user) | Day list by default; week as seven day-headed lists [ASSUMPTION] | Bottom sheet |
+
+Tabs stay in the top bar at every width [ASSUMPTION]. Manage rooms works on phone as a simple list, but is designed laptop-first [ASSUMPTION].

+
+1. Opens the app on their phone. It remembers their name, so Rooms opens on Leeds, today.
+2. The next free rooms list shows rooms free from 14:00. They choose "1 h".
+3. They tap "Book" on a room showing "Free until 16:00".
+4. The booking sheet opens with room, 14:00–15:00 and "{Name}'s meeting" filled in. They add two colleagues as attendees.
+5. **Climax:** they tap "Book". "Booked. {Room}, 14:00–15:00." The booking appears in their My bookings and in both attendees' calendars. Two taps, plus the attendees they chose to add.
+
+Failure: someone booked that room a moment earlier. The sheet shows the refusal and three rooms still free at 14:00; one tap books another.
+

+
+1. On their laptop, Rooms opens on Manchester. They switch the office to London and the date to next Tuesday.
+2. The day grid shows London's rooms; they tap a free slot at 10:00.
+3. In the sheet they set the length to 2 h and add London colleagues.
+4. **Climax:** "Book". The slot turns solid navy, with their title on it, in London's grid.
+

+
+1. They open My bookings, week view.
+2. They tap a meeting; details show "Change" and "Cancel booking".
+3. "Change": they move it to Thursday 11:00; the app checks the room is free and saves.
+4. They open another meeting and tap "Cancel booking", then confirm.
+5. **Climax:** the week view updates at once; the cancelled room shows as free in Rooms for everyone.
+

+
+1. They open Manage rooms; the table lists London's rooms.
+2. "Close" on a room: the confirmation says it has 3 future bookings and that closing stops new bookings.
+3. They confirm; the room shows "Closed" in the grid. Later they "Add room" for a newly fitted room.

+5. **Climax:** the grid shows the closed room greyed out, the new room open, and the urgent slot free. The room list matches reality.

+- Exact company navy and any logo: to be supplied; DESIGN.md hex values stand until then.

+1. On their laptop, Rooms opens on Manchester. They switch the office to London and the date to next Tuesday.
+2. The day grid shows London's rooms; they tap a free slot at 10:00.
+3. In the sheet they set the length to 2 h and add London colleagues.
+4. **Climax:** "Book". The slot turns solid navy, with their title on it, in London's grid.
+
+### UJ-3: An organiser moves and cancels meetings
+
+1. They open My bookings, week view.
+2. They tap a meeting; details show "Change" and "Cancel booking".
+3. "Change": they move it to Thursday 11:00; the app checks the room is free and saves.
+4. They open another meeting and tap "Cancel booking", then confirm.
+5. **Climax:** the week view updates at once; the cancelled room shows as free in Rooms for everyone.
+
+### UJ-4: A London office manager closes a room for repairs
+
+1. They open Manage rooms; the table lists London's rooms.
+2. "Close" on a room: the confirmation says it has 3 future bookings and that closing stops new bookings.
+3. They confirm; the room shows "Closed" in the grid. Later they "Add room" for a newly fitted room.
+4. From the Rooms grid they tap someone's booking in a London room; as an office manager they see "Change" and "Cancel booking" and move it to free the slot for an urgent meeting.
+5. **Climax:** the grid shows the closed room greyed out, the new room open, and the urgent slot free. The room list matches reality.
+
+## Open items
+
+- What happens to future bookings when a room closes is decided in the rooms epic (PRD FR-5); the UX only shows the count.
+- Exact company navy and any logo: to be supplied; DESIGN.md hex values stand until then.
